title: Editing window, versions, pinned human edits, lock time
description:
A Delivery is a draft with an edit window, not a one-shot. The window runs from creation to releaseAt and is set per kind and per channel as data (a weekly newsletter has a week; a story post may have twenty minutes). The machine drafts, people edit; every edit is a new saved version of the Delivery text and none is overwritten. Blocks and lines a person changed are marked owner: human, pinned, and a later machine redraft never overwrites a pinned block (same rule as Story translations). A Delivery may hold several candidate texts or images, one chosen and the others kept (basis for later A/B). At a set time before releaseAt the Delivery locks for the send job and the last approved version is sent; a late edit needs an explicit unlock; the attempt log records which version was sent. Where approval is soft or hard nothing is sent that no person looked at; for none the machine draft goes at releaseAt.

**Acceptance criteria**
- New Gherkin features (to be written with the slice): Edit window and versions (every edit a new version, earlier versions kept); Pinned human edits survive a redraft; Candidate versions (choose one, keep others); Lock time and unlock (late edit refused until unlocked; attempt records the version sent); Nothing unseen is sent under soft or hard approval.
- Window length is data per kind and channel, not code.
- Text and versions live in S3; the row holds keys and hashes.
- Operations available from newsroom and CLI from the one operation table.

Design: ~/Projects/papyrus-announcement-delivery-design.md. X feed stays OFF. No real email addresses in specs or fixtures. Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs.

**Section 13 additions (2026-11-16, always-on agent review; changes C, E, K)**
- Blocked by the review-policy task (PPY-97c0f2), which defines who may unlock and edit.
- A Delivery save names the version it replaces. A stale save is refused with an answer that names the version that replaced it (as guidelines and image profiles already do). A refused machine redraft is dropped: the person's version is newer.
- A lock is a fact, not something held: `lockedAt` and `lockedVersion` on the Delivery. Unlock is an event from a person. Nothing expires and nothing waits holding a lease; a person who never answers blocks only that Delivery. `lockAt` (from PPY-3792dd) is the time the lock is raised; when it fires it only raises an event and the worker re-reads the record.
- Soft review needs no time of its own: silence until `lockAt` is the rule.
**Acceptance criteria (added)**
- Gherkin: two saves against one version, the second refused, naming the version that replaced it.
- Gherkin: a machine redraft against a stale version is dropped and the person's version stays.
- Gherkin: lock writes lockedAt and lockedVersion; the lockedVersion is the version sent; a late edit after the lock needs an explicit unlock by a person.

**Always-on agent standard (2026-11-16; design `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md`)**
- Lock and release times are follow-up timers (PPY-3ff011); a time that fires only raises a wake and the run re-checks everything.
- **Soft review with silence** (gap found in PR #1618: `releasable` returns true at the lock time, but `lock` refuses when no version is approved). At the lock time under `soft` with no person's approval, the engine approves the current version as the policy (`approvedBy` names the policy), then locks, in one conditional write.
- An edit made while an attempt is open does not change that attempt; it is saved as a preferred version (PPY-75a314).
**Acceptance criteria (added)**
- Gherkin: under `soft` with nobody acting, the current version is approved by policy and locked at the lock time, and the record says so; an edit and a lock at the same moment leave exactly one winner; an edit during an open attempt becomes a preferred version.

Built: Delivery text versions in S3 (row holds key, hash, author, replaced version), stale save refused naming the replacing version, machine redraft dropped, pinned human blocks that a redraft keeps, candidates (choose one, keep the rest), lockedAt/lockedVersion raised at lockAt by a follow-up timer wake, soft silence approved by the policy and locked in one write, hard with no approval flagged once, late edit needs a person's unlock, an edit during an open attempt saved as a preferred version, attempt log records the version sent, window lengths as data per kind and channel in the announcement settings, operations (versions, draft, candidate choose, pinned, unlock) from the one operation table. Left: a person's CLI unlock cannot move the follow-up timer (no scheduler rights on that lane; needs the deliver runtime deploy), console editing UI, channel checks of edited words.
